real_qa.q: What does AASHTO and ASTM prohibit regarding the use of AI in creating derivative works from their standards?
real_qa.r: Both AASHTO and ASTM organizations prohibit the use of AI to create derivative work products like internal exams, policies, procedures, templates, or records based on their standards. Violating this restriction means violating your user agreement with them and their rights to maintain their own copyright.
real_qa.requete: AASHTO ASTM AI derivative works prohibition

real_qa.q: What are red flags that laboratories are submitting AI-generated documentation to the AASHTO accreditation program?
real_qa.r: Red flags include obviously irrelevant equipment requirements (such as a five-gallon bucket for unrelated procedures or a shovel for thermometer standardization), and AI-generated procedures and records that are excessively long (seven pages instead of one) with irrelevant information and nonsensical details that no human expert would include.
real_qa.requete: AASHTO AI generated documents red flags

real_qa.q: What are acceptable uses of AI tools for laboratories maintaining AASHTO accreditation?
real_qa.r: Acceptable uses include helping format or shuffle existing exam questions that a laboratory has already created themselves, such as using Copilot to rearrange answer order so patterns are not obvious. However, you cannot ask AI to create new derivative works from standards—only assist with reformatting your own original content.
real_qa.requete: AASHTO AI acceptable uses laboratories formatting

real_qa.q: Why is AI-generated documentation in testing laboratories a public safety concern for infrastructure?
real_qa.r: If contractors and testing labs both use AI without proper human oversight and expertise, the data and materials used in buildings, bridges, and roads may not be accurately measured or verified. This creates risk for anybody using the end product, as materials testing validates structural integrity and safety compliance.
real_qa.requete: AI testing labs public safety buildings bridges roads

real_qa.q: What standard requires laboratory technicians to pass a written exam under AASHTO accreditation?
real_qa.r: ASTM D3740 requires laboratory technicians to pass a written exam. One challenge laboratories face is keeping those exams up to date and shuffling questions so patterns do not become obvious to repeat test-takers.
real_qa.requete: ASTM D3740 laboratory technician written exam requirement
